t.E212.agn: In 2016 EFSA set a combined acceptable daily intake (ADI) for benzoic acid and its salts of 5 mg/kg body weight, expressed as benzoic acid; it stated that this limit may be exceeded in young children who consume a lot of the same brand, particularly from flavoured drinks. When present together with vitamin C (ascorbic acid), small amounts of benzene may form in drinks; the FDA monitored this issue and manufacturers adjusted their formulations.
t.E212.eff.0.t: The daily limit may be exceeded, particularly from flavoured drinks
t.E212.eff.0.w: Young children who consume a lot of the same brand
t.E212.eval: Benzoates may form benzene in drinks containing vitamin C (ascorbic acid) (benzene is IARC Group 1); the industry therefore adjusted its formulations. The mixtures in the Southampton study also contained sodium benzoate, but the EU does not require a separate warning label for this substance.
t.E212.prod: Produced by chemical synthesis; benzoic acid also occurs naturally in some fruits.
t.E212.pw.0: According to EFSA, the daily limit may be exceeded in young children who consume a lot of the same brand.
t.E212.regx.0: Re-evaluated; combined ADI for benzoates 5 mg/kg (as benzoic acid).
t.E212.summary: The potassium salt of benzoic acid. Used as a preservative in acidic drinks and sauces.
t.E212.what: Extends shelf life by delaying spoilage caused by microorganisms; works best in acidic products.
